languages.claim: JavaScript V1 Ring 2 medium-programs are verified bidirectionally through canonical IR to Lua, JavaScript, and LUASCRIPT .ls outputs.

parser.note: The V1 Ring 2 manifest parses JavaScript fixtures through the current JS-to-IR compiler.

lowering.note: Fixtures lower to canonical IR and emit all V1 Ring 2 targets.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, and supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls.

runtime.note: Native and emitted targets execute and compare stdout.

integration.note: Ring 2 covers closure state, nested object state, nested loops, break/continue, short-circuit side effects, and explicit unsupported diagnostics.

languages.claim: TypeScript V0.25 typed-JS small-programs are verified through canonical IR to Lua, JavaScript, LUASCRIPT .ls, and Python outputs.

parser.note: The V0.25 manifest parses TypeScript through the TypeScript compiler API, validates the supported slice, erases runtime-neutral type syntax, and lowers the generated JavaScript to canonical IR.

lowering.note: Fixtures lower typed locals, typed functions, arrays, interface/type-alias annotations, object mutation, loops, break/continue, string length/indexing, and boolean short-circuit behavior.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls, and Python outputs.

runtime.note: Native TypeScript is executed by transpiling the verified slice to JavaScript and running Node; every emitted target executes and compares stdout.

integration.note: Unsupported TypeScript features outside V0.25, including classes, enums, generics, and imports, fail with explicit diagnostics.

languages.claim: LUASCRIPT .ls V1 Ring 2 JS-like medium-programs are verified through the shared bidirectional gate and actual-program suite.

parser.note: The V1 Ring 2 manifest treats supported .ls as JS-like source for canonical IR.

lowering.note: Fixtures lower to canonical IR and actual .ls programs continue through the compiler.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, and supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls.

runtime.note: Native .ls and emitted targets execute and compare stdout.

integration.note: Ring 2 covers closure state, nested object state, nested loops, break/continue, short-circuit side effects, and actual-program coverage through language:luascript:bidirectional and clarity:dogfood.

languages.claim: Lua input V2 is requalified for a documented small-program slice through canonical IR to Lua, JavaScript, and LUASCRIPT .ls outputs.

parser.note: luaparse-backed Lua fixtures are parsed by the strict V2 gate.

lowering.note: Lua fixtures lower to canonical IR artifacts with object-style roots for current emitters.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, and supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls.

runtime.note: Lua output, JavaScript output, and emitted .ls compiled to Lua execute and compare stdout.

integration.note: The Lua input fixture suite remains a separate strict gate in language:lua:bidirectional and test:lua-input.

languages.claim: Python V1.2 small-programs are verified bidirectionally through canonical IR to Lua, JavaScript, LUASCRIPT .ls, and Python output.

parser.note: The V1.2 manifest parses Python fixtures through CPython ast and the Python-to-IR compiler.

lowering.note: Fixtures lower to canonical IR and retain Python source semantics for the V1.2 slice.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls, and Python.

runtime.note: Native Python and every emitted target execute and compare stdout.

integration.note: Unsupported Python V1.2-outside features are covered by explicit diagnostics plus JS/Lua/LUASCRIPT canonical reverse fixtures.

languages.claim: Ruby V0.6 has a target-runtime canonical-IR lane plus a narrow native Ruby bidirectional gate; broad Ruby remains unqualified.

parser.note: The V0.6 manifest parses method-oriented Ruby fixtures through RubyToIRCompiler.

lowering.note: The V0.6 slice lowers methods, locals, arithmetic, while/if control flow, simple array iteration, indexed reads/writes, simple hashes, hash mutation, inclusive numeric ranges, boolean flow, break/next, string indexing/length, length/size, math calls, and puts output into canonical IR.

emitter.note: The gate emits Lua, JavaScript, supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls, Python, and C# outputs that execute and compare stdout.

runtime.note: Native Ruby execution runs the V0.6 fixture slice through ruby and compares stdout.

integration.note: Native Ruby plus emitted Lua, JavaScript, supported JS-like LUASCRIPT .ls, Python, and C# outputs execute for the named slice; broader Ruby remains outside the claim.
